notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main, so there was no candidate id to create from. The schema follows the arm9/MaterialChanger and arm9/dCcAc_c entries, which took the same route; this entry subsumes the earlier arm9/Model, arm9/ModelAnim and arm9/BlendModelAnim manifests, whose runs are slices of this one.

The MI classes' destructors are written as free functions spelling the member dtor's synthesized steps, not member definitions: defining ~ModelAnim, ~BlendModelAnim or ~ModelAnim2 emits that class's whole MI vtable group, whose _ZTS/_ZTI records spell the project name where the cartridge homes the dExt* one (notes/model-rtti-names.md). Emitted records under project spellings have no byte-compatible ROM home -- deadstrip-data compares differ, externalized_output requires literal-identical copies -- the forced split the previous arm9/BlendModelAnim manifest documented, resolved here by writing the synthesized bodies (two vptr stores, secondary base at +0x50 destroyed via its D2, primary base via Model/ModelAnim's D2, D0 appending the class operator delete). The base-destruction calls keep mangled spellings: a qualified-id destructor call (thiz->ModelAnim::~ModelAnim()) devirtualizes to the complete-object D1, where base-subobject destruction needs the D2 the cartridge calls; otherAnim's member destruction does need D1 and keeps the qualified-id spelling.

The six _ZThn80_ destructor thunks at 0x02017168..0x020171c8 keep their enrolled shards: only a member dtor definition emits adjustor thunks, and a written adjustor compiles to `bx ip` rather than the cartridge's `ldr ip; add r0,r0,ip; b`. The shard member definitions emit the full group in their own objects and objisolate keeps the bound thunk -- the same mechanism that already produced them.

SetAnim and Func_020162C4 stay mangled extern "C" definitions (wall 6az, notes/mwccarm-codegen.md): the real signatures carry Fix12<int> by value, and their dExtFrameCtrl_c::SetAnimation calls keep the mangled spelling because passing the real declaration's Fix12<int> by value homes the argument to the caller's stack.

The file is written ROM-descending because mwccarm emits .text in reverse source order under default deferred codegen; the emitted object carries the 62 licensed functions ascending 0x02016254..0x02017168.

The TU compiles with #pragma RTTI off: every class in the family has its cartridge _ZTS/_ZTI records homed under a coined dExt* name (notes/model-rtti-names.md), so no RTTI records are emitted and the vtables' preamble typeinfo words deadstrip with the rest of the .data output -- the same lever the MaterialChanger and ShadowModel folds use for the identical coined-name situation.

common.h precedes the class headers so this TU sees the flat Matrix4x3 { s32 m[12]; } spelling: Model's ctor `mat4x3 = IDENTITY_MATRIX4X3` block-moves twelve words under it, where the structured Matrix3x3+Vector3 spelling scalarizes into a longer sequence. Virtual10 keeps the same flat view for its twelve-word copy into data.transforms.

Several local externs deliberately keep the call-site spellings the shards carried: func_02045e2c's fourth parameter is int where its definition takes short (the computed argument produces the ROM's codegen), and func_02045e70/func_02045ef8/func_02045f80/func_0204605c stay one-parameter under-declarations -- the +8 self-adjusting thunks forward their callers' r1/r2 untouched, which C cannot express. These are banked decl-agreement rows.
